{{Short description|British physicist}}
'''Franz Ferdinand Heymann''' (17 August 1924 – 28 March 2005)<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ucl.ac.uk/news/deaths/2005 |title=Deaths - 2005 |publisher=ucl.ac.uk |accessdate=November 27, 2017}}</ref> was a British physicist who served as [[Quain Professor]] from 1975–80 at [[University College London]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.hep.ucl.ac.uk/history/Franz/ |title=Franz Heymann profile|publisher=ucl.ac.uk |accessdate=November 27, 2017}}</ref> He was featured in ''Who's Who in British Scientists'', ''Who's Who in Atoms'' and ''Who's Who in Technology''.<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=V2lIAQAAIAAJ&q=Franz+Ferdinand+Heymann+professor ''Who's Who in Atoms''], 1969.</ref><ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=Vws5AAAAIAAJ&q=Franz+Ferdinand+Heymann+professor ''Who's Who in British Scientists''], 1971.</ref>

==Education and early career==
He earned his BsC at [[University of Cape Town]] in 1944 and his Ph.D at [[University College London]] in 1953.

At University College London, he was Assistant Lecturer, Department of Physics (1950-1952); Lecturer (1952-1960); Professor (1966-1972); and Professor, Department of Physics & Astronomy (1975-1987).<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=V3hRAAAAMAAJ&q=Franz+Ferdinand+Heymann+professor ''Who's Who in Technology''], Volumes 1-3, 1984.</ref>

==Selected publications==
* "Parity conservation in n° production by neutrons", Nuovo Cim 1959
* "Quenching of ortho positronium in helium", Proc R Soc 1962
